summary: The Astronaut Health Monitoring System is a project designed to monitor the health of astronauts during space missions. In space, low gravity and environmental changes can affect the human body, including heart rate, oxygen levels, body temperature, and movement. Our project uses an ESP32 microcontroller and different sensors to collect health data in real time. The MAX30102 sensor measures heart rate and blood oxygen level (SpO2), the MPU6050 detects body movement, and the DS18B20 measures temperature. An OLED display shows the sensor readings. The ESP32 collects and processes the data, then sends it to a software dashboard. The dashboard displays heart rate, oxygen level, body movement, temperature, and live graphs. This helps users monitor health details easily and identify unusual readings. The system provides continuous monitoring and supports early detection of possible health problems. In the future, cloud storage, AI analysis, wireless communication, and automatic emergency alerts can be added. This project combines hardware and software to support astronaut health and safety during space missions.
details:
Components Required

  1. ESP32 Module: Acts as the main controller and processes sensor data.
  2. MAX30102 Heart Rate and SpO₂ Sensor: Measures heart rate (BPM) and blood oxygen level (SpO₂).
  3. DS18B20 Temperature Sensor: Measures body temperature in Celsius.
  4. Breadboard: Helps connect the components without soldering.
  5. 4.7kΩ Resistor: Used as a pull-up resistor for the DS18B20 sensor.
  6. Jumper Wires (Male-to-Male): Used to connect the sensors to the ESP32.

Software Required

  1. Arduino IDE: Used to write, compile, and upload the program to the ESP32.
  2. MAX30102 Sensor Library: Helps read heart rate and SpO₂ values.
  3. OneWire Library: Supports communication with the DS18B20 sensor.
  4. DallasTemperature Library: Helps read temperature data from the DS18B20 sensor.

Final Output – Three Health Values

The system displays three important health readings:

  • ❤️ Heart Rate (BPM): Shows the number of heartbeats per minute.
  • 🫁 SpO₂ (%): Shows the estimated oxygen level in the blood.
  • 🌡️ Body Temperature (°C): Shows the measured temperature.

Overall Output: The ESP32 collects data from the sensors and displays heart rate, blood oxygen level, and temperature in real time. These readings help monitor the astronaut's basic health condition during space missions.
